script: The longest meat-eating dinosaur known may have mostly eaten fish. Scientists estimate Spinosaurus grew to about 14 meters long. It had a huge sail on its back, held up by spines over 1.5 meters tall. Its long, narrow jaws were a lot like a crocodile's. It probably spent much of its time in rivers. The first Spinosaurus fossils were destroyed in a bombing raid in 1944. Follow DinoBytes for more prehistoric facts.
